# Four filings, zero merges: where three agents actually sit this week

#mcp #opensource #webdev #showdev

Between 1 and 3 October 2026 I filed the same three names into four public catalogs. None of those pull requests is merged. The software is already callable. The directories are not.

The three names are WARDEN (an MCP firewall for tool definitions), HISTOR (a signed log of what remote MCP servers advertised), and AIMarket Hub (the catalog they sit in). This is a status note, not a launch.

## What was filed

Where  | When  | What  | State on 3 Oct 2026
--- | --- | --- | ---
Docker MCP Registry #5364  | 1 Oct  | WARDEN, local server, package 0.8.2  | Open
Docker MCP Registry #5365  | 1 Oct  | Hub at `https://modelmarket.dev/mcp`  | Open
awesome-erc8004 #120  | 1 Oct  | Hub, HISTOR, WARDEN as ERC-8004 agents on Base  | Open
coinbase/x402 #373  | 2 Oct  | Six paid routes under Services/Endpoints  | Open
The routes themselves do not wait on that page.

Settlement in the pull request goes through the CDP facilitator. That is a payment rail for those six URLs. It is not a claim that the Hub homepage is a busy market.

## The on-chain IDs are published. The awesome-list is not.

modelmarket.dev/.well-known/agent-registration.json names three agents on Base, registry `eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432`:

  * AIMarket Hub — agent 96682
  * HISTOR — agent 96683
  * WARDEN — agent 96684

The awesome-erc8004 pull request is a README link to those IDs. Merging it changes a list. It does not create the agents. Leaving it open does not delete them either. A scan link from the pull request: 8004scan.io/agents/base/96682.

## What I will not say until a maintainer clicks merge

  * WARDEN is not in the Docker MCP catalog yet.
  * The Hub is not in that catalog yet.
  * AIMarket is not on the x402 ecosystem page yet.
  * The three names are not in awesome-erc8004 yet.
  * Cline has a submission issue, not a marketplace card.

The useful check is the thing you can call: the npm package, the MCP URL, the a2mcp list, the registration file. The catalogs are a paper trail. This week the paper is still in review.

## If you publish an MCP server

  * List your tools without a key. Ask for it when a tool is called. Do not check its format at startup.
  * Default to stdio, or name the flag that turns it on in your error text.
  * Pin `mcp<2` or move to 2.x.
  * Ship one command. If your package also has a CLI, put `mcp` in the server's name.
  * Keep stdout for JSON-RPC. Logs, banners and help go to stderr.
  * Set `Requires-Python` honestly and publish wheels.
  * Do not download binaries at install or startup. Ship them as per-platform optional dependencies.

## Check what you run

Every package's record is public on histor.modelmarket.dev: its tools, what it asked for, what it touched, which image it ran in. WARDEN reads the same log. `npx -y @aimarket/warden@0.15.0 scan --histor` asks HISTOR, for every server in your Claude, Cursor or VS Code config, whether you get the tool set HISTOR recorded, and shows what its package did in the sandbox. For a package, that is the set its sandbox got. A launcher whose program is installed on your machine lists another one; its publisher can now declare that set in the server's registry entry, and HISTOR shows it as the publisher's word.

We build HISTOR and WARDEN. The numbers are a snapshot of 13 October 2026; the crawl continues, so the site will have moved on. No package is named here. The method and the observer's code are in alexar76/histor (`docs/architecture.md`, `sandbox/histor_observe.py`).

Edited 14 October 2026: the WARDEN sentence above said it checks "whether you get the tool set everyone else gets". For a launcher package that is not one set, as a reader pointed out in the comments; it now says what HISTOR compares with.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Never calls a server safe.

The timeline and `package_observations.jsonl.gz` expose the version, observer, image, runtime, entry and supplied configuration. Older rows remain `null` where the facts were never recorded.

In version 0.4.2, we also shipped four reviewed launch defaults:

Package  | Supplied test configuration
--- | ---
Filesystem  | The disposable container's `/work/app` directory
Azure DevOps  | A synthetic organization, envvar authentication and a placeholder token
LaunchDarkly  | The `start` command, stdio transport and a per-run placeholder
Figma  | `--stdio` and a placeholder environment variable

Explicit registry arguments take precedence. A previous failure can retry with the new configuration while retaining its earlier observation. The sandbox generates placeholder values locally; it receives no real credentials and gains no internet route.

We fixed another attribution error: when the observer omits its resolved version, the reader now leaves it unknown instead of substituting the version requested by the crawler.

These follow-up changes ship in aimarket-histor 0.4.2. Both standalone sandbox observers were updated before the production HISTOR service on 27 October. The local HISTOR suite passed 610 tests, with 210 PostgreSQL cases skipped without a test database, one optional token-count case skipped without `tiktoken`, and 12 integration cases deselected. The new profile regressions use synthetic package responses and a stubbed container boundary. They do not establish four new successful captures of current upstream packages. Supabase and other services requiring a real authenticated network session can still remain unobserved.
